chain.label: Inadequate FAA oversight of Fresh Air's operations
chain.trigger: the POI had never directly observed Fresh Air's operation, he was unaware that the airplanes were being operated contrary to the limitations outlined in the FAA-approved AFM

chain.label: Airplane departed overweight with ADI and autofeather systems off
chain.trigger: the accident airplane exceeded the maximum allowable takeoff weight of 40,900 lbs

caused_by.evidence: Fresh Air pilots were operating the airplane with the autofeather and antidetonation injection systems off, yet using a higher gross takeoff weight than permitted with these systems off...the POI was unaware

chain.label: Oil or fuel leak ignited at the augmentor/muffler junction
chain.trigger: a leak in the vicinity of the augmentor/muffler junction allowed the fire to exit the junction and damage portions of the right wing

chain.label: In-flight fire in the right augmentor
chain.trigger: fire and thermal damage to the airframe on the airplane's right wing rear spar, nacelle aft of the power section, and in the vicinity of the junction between the augmentor assemblies and the exhaust muffler assembly

caused_by.evidence: oil or fuel leaks into the exhaust system are capable of igniting in the presence of the high heat within the augmentors and would have led to the exhaust fire

chain.label: Crew shut down the right engine but erroneously feathered the left propeller
chain.trigger: the left propeller was found feathered at impact...Because the autofeather system was not activated, the flight crew had to manually feather the propeller and likely manually selected the left propeller to feather

caused_by.evidence: the flight crew likely intended to shut down the right engine...they likely suspected an engine fire due to the smoke

chain.label: Captain experiencing acute sleep loss
chain.trigger: the captain was likely suffering from acute sleep loss at the time of the accident, which would have negatively affected his ability to guide the first officer in properly handling the emergency

chain.label: Flight crew failed to maintain adequate airspeed
chain.trigger: the probable cause of this accident was the flight crew's failure to maintain adequate airspeed after shutting down the right engine due to an in-flight fire in one of the right augmentors

caused_by.evidence: the right propeller's pitch was consistent with a high rotation/takeoff power setting...at least one engine was generating thrust until near the end of the flight
the airplane was above the maximum allowable takeoff weight, making it even more difficult for the flight crew to maintain altitude or airspeed when operating with one engine
this sleep loss would have led to degraded decision-making, inadequate risk assessment, and reduced leadership, all skills that would have been critical during the accident sequence

chain.label: Aerodynamic stall or loss of directional control
chain.trigger: The failure to maintain airspeed resulted in either an aerodynamic stall or a loss of directional control

caused_by.evidence: the last estimated airspeed was 88 knots, 9 knots below the published stall speed for level flight and close to the 87-knot air minimum control speed

chain.label: Airplane struck trees and crashed into the lagoon
chain.trigger: the airplane struck trees with its right wingtip and crashed into the lagoon while traveling in a northerly direction

caused_by.evidence: Radar contact was lost with the airplane at 100 ft as it continued the right turn; shortly thereafter, the airplane struck trees

chain.label: Both pilots fatally injured
chain.trigger: The two pilots died, and the airplane was destroyed by impact forces

caused_by.evidence: The two pilots died, and the airplane was destroyed by impact forces
